hooks.line: I am so mad, and this is exactly why you read the reviews before you buy another foundation. Because I bought this FACELOVE stick that everyone would not stop raving about, and I am going to be returning it.

concepts.frame1: her bare, red-cheeked face close to the lens, the FACELOVE carton held up beside it and tapped twice, sticker 'I'm so mad 😡'
concepts.stakes: she is furious at a product everyone loves
concepts.turn: '…and I am going to be returning it' — the carton drops into a return mailer

concepts.frame1: the return mailer slapped down on the white vanity, the carton dropped into it from above
concepts.stakes: the product is already going back
concepts.turn: cut up to her cross face for the first line

concepts.frame1: close on her red cheek, one finger pointing at the redness
concepts.stakes: the problem she has lived with

concepts.frame1: she walks out of a department store beauty hall, shopping bag swinging, jaw set
concepts.turn: cut to her at home, still mad

concepts.frame1: a pile of half-used foundation bottles swept off the vanity into a bin
concepts.stakes: years of money on the wrong shades
concepts.turn: she holds up the one stick she is 'returning'

hooks.line: Okay, I need to vent. I finally found a foundation that actually matches my redness, and I am sending it back. Here is why.

concepts.frame1: screech of tape: her hands tape shut a grey return mailer with the FACELOVE carton inside, then she looks straight up at the lens
concepts.stakes: she's sending back the one that worked
concepts.turn: 'Here is why.' — straight into the body

concepts.frame1: half her face: one cheek even, the other still red, she points at both
concepts.stakes: it worked — so why return it?

concepts.frame1: she rolls her eyes and drops into the vanity chair, bare-faced
concepts.turn: she lifts the stick to the lens

concepts.frame1: a post-office counter, the parcel slid across
close on the stick in her fist, knuckles tight

hooks.line: Every makeup counter told me nothing would ever match my redness. So why am I returning the one stick that finally did?

concepts.frame1: over the saleswoman's shoulder at the makeup counter: a bottle held to her red jaw, three wrong swatches, a slow head shake
concepts.stakes: the experts gave up on her skin
concepts.turn: cut to her at home holding the stick: 'So why am I returning…'

concepts.frame1: macro: the white balm laid across her red cheek, the brush turning it to her exact shade
concepts.stakes: proof it did what the counter said was impossible
concepts.turn: her face, puzzled at her own question

concepts.frame1: a row of wrong-shade bottles on the counter, each one too pink or too orange against her jaw
concepts.turn: the stick against her jaw — perfect

concepts.frame1: she shrugs at the lens holding the stick, eyebrows up
a shopping bag of returned foundations on the bed

groups.idea: the fake-out: every 'it's not because' is the stick working on her real skin, then the counter woman who said it couldn't

rows.line: And it is not because it goes on pure white

candidates.picture: the balm's flat crest pressing onto her bare, red cheekbone and drawing one clean white stripe
the uncapped stick held up white end to the lens
a macro of the white balm crest alone, no skin

rows.line: and then turns into my exact shade

candidates.picture: side-on macro: the brush circles through the white stripe and the white becomes her olive skin right behind the crown, still white ahead of it
two stills: white stripe, then blended cheek, cut together
the brush end held up to the lens

rows.line: and melts in like it was made for my skin.

candidates.picture: two fingertips pat the finished cheek, then her eyes come to the lens, quietly pleased; her crow's feet still there
a slow look at the blended cheek in window light
the capped stick set down on the vanity

rows.line: told me my redness was too tricky to match and I should not bother.

candidates.picture: over the saleswoman's shoulder: she holds a bottle beside the creator's red jaw, three swatch stripes matching nothing, and slowly shakes her head
three beige swatch stripes on her red jaw, none matching
the whole beauty hall, the creator small at one counter

groups.idea: the reasons pile up: each problem named is covered on her face, then the world notices

rows.line: It is not because it covered the redness,

candidates.picture: her cheek half done — even on one side, red on the other — the brush stopping right on the border
the whole cheek blended, red gone
a close-up of red skin

rows.line: the hyperpigmentation, the old post-acne marks,

candidates.picture: from under the jaw: the balm crest glides over the small brown marks, a thin white line laid on them
the marks, then the blended jaw
a macro of the brown marks alone

rows.line: and every tired line and dark circle

candidates.picture: the brush pats under her eye: the dark circle evens out while the crow's feet stay exactly where they were
her tired eye in the mirror before
a macro of the dark circle

rows.line: I have been hiding for years, in one swipe.

candidates.picture: one brush swipe across her cheekbone, then her whole face even, every line still there, eyes to the lens
her raised-eyebrow look to the lens
the concealer and three bottles she used to hide it pushed into a drawer

rows.line: And it is definitely not because three of my friends this week

candidates.picture: over her shoulder at the café: three friends lean in at once, coffees in hand, eyes on her face
one friend's eyebrows going up
three coffees on a table
the auburn friend touches her own cheek with two fingers and raises her brows, asking
the stick slid across the café table
the friend's face from the creator's seat, mouthing the question

groups.idea: the easy morning: one swipe at the hall mirror and out of the door

rows.line: throw this one stick on before the grocery store,

candidates.picture: keys on one finger, one swipe across her cheek in the round brass hall mirror, cap on
the grocery store aisle
the stick in her tote bag

rows.line: and feel completely confident walking out the door.

candidates.picture: from low on the path: she pulls the door shut and walks two steps toward us in the morning sun, chin up
her smile in the car mirror
a front door opening

groups.idea: the twist: the deal laid out on her vanity, and the one stick going back

rows.line: Two full Foundation Sticks for almost the price of one,

two sticks on a white background
one stick, then two

level with the vanity: her hand sets the primer and the small gift box beside the two sticks, the box lid ajar on a fold of tissue paper
the primer tube alone

rows.line: and a full thirty day money back guarantee.

candidates.picture: low on the vanity: her hand slides the whole bundle — two sticks, primer, gift box — toward the lens
a calendar page with thirty days
her shrug — nothing to lose

rows.line: and buying the deal like I should have.

candidates.picture: on her front step in the morning sun she picks up the delivery box and tucks it under her arm with a grin
the bundle unboxed on the vanity
a parcel on a doorstep

groups.idea: the formula, not her skin: her finished face and the stick in one frame

rows.line: It was never your skin. It was the formula.
